text:
olivia: quick heads-up — ran a cross-model RoPE scale pass (linear / ntk / yarn) to investigate the recent perf cliff on longctx for mixtral-8x. seeing consistent perplexity bump around 30–35k tokens on ntk variants and throughput regressions on linear at >16k.

raj: can you paste the minimal repro? where are we seeing the throughput hit — kernel scheduling or kv cache churn? :thinking:

olivia: minimal repro below. ran on dedicated GPU pool (A100 80G), config pinned to mixtral-8x, batch=1 -> long tail single-request latency.

```
# repro
SERVE_BIN=./bin/serve_prof
$SERVE_BIN --model=mixtral-8x --rope=ntk --seq=32768 --batching=continuous --profile=kernel,kv --runs=20
```

mike: thanks. quick profiler dump shows kernel choice oscillating between headpack and fallback GEMM at sequence grow. suspects: kernel picker cost model uses wrong position-length priors so it keeps flipping. log snippet: 

```
[profiler] choose_kernel(): candidate=headpack cost=12.4ms
[profiler] choose_kernel(): candidate=gpu_gemm cost=11.2ms
[cache] kv_slot_miss++ -> evict: 3 entries
[perf] token_latency p95=142ms -> 212ms
```

sarah: interesting — the kv evictions coincide with the kernel flips. if the kv cache is being partially evicted at those sequence lengths, we get more cache warmup and the kernel cost estimates change dramatically. might be a batching heuristic + kv eviction interaction.

raj: did you try disabling prefix caching to rule out cache eviction thrash? also what quantization/heads config used? mixtral-8x has head_kv_dim=64 vs qwen-like 80, could be sensitive.

olivia: ran 3 quick variants: (1) prefix_cache=on (default), (2) prefix_cache=off, (3) prefix_cache=on + kv_reserve=0.2 (reserve fraction). results:
- prefix_cache=off: throughput improved slightly but perplexity bump still present for ntk at 32k.
- kv_reserve=0.2: p95 latency reduced and kernel selection stabilized around headpack.

mike: that suggests the cache capacity threshold in our heuristic is too tight for the headpack kernel's memory working set. headpack expects KV persistence; if entries get evicted it becomes advantageous to switch to GEMM which recomputes some state. The picker mistakenly focuses on raw kernel latency without amortized warmup cost.

raj: can we adjust kernel picker to incorporate amortized prefix-reuse score? e.g., score = latency_est + alpha * (1 - hit_rate) * warmup_penalty where hit_rate from recent KV telemetry. small alpha should bias towards stable kernels when hit_rate is high.

olivia: implemented prototype patch locally: added recent_kv_hit_rate window=300s and warmup_penalty=40ms. quick smoke shows much fewer flips.

infra-bot: canary deploy queued -> canary-serve-2026-03-18-01 : running 10% traffic on dedicated pool.

sarah: any per-model safe ranges for RoPE scaling? Mixtral seems safe up to 16k linear, 24k yarn with kv_reserve=0.2; ntk shows quality regressions >28k on mixtral-8x (perplexity +1.8). Llama-3 13B tolerates linear to 20k but ntk gives worse long-term stability. Qwen-7B is surprisingly robust to yarn up to 40k but head dims differ so kernel behavior differs.

mike: logging this as recommended runtime defaults per-model:
- mixtral-8x: default_rope_variant=yarn, safe_max_seq=24576, kv_reserve=0.2, kernel_picker_alpha=0.15
- llama-3-13b: default_rope_variant=linear, safe_max_seq=20480, kv_reserve=0.15
- qwen-7b: default_rope_variant=yarn, safe_max_seq=40960, kv_reserve=0.12

raj: please open a small PR with the picker change + model-default overrides. also add a perf-test in CI that runs a short longctx sweep (8k,16k,24k,32k) to catch regressions.

olivia: will do. attaching perf plot (quick summary): p95 latency vs seq length for ntk vs linear vs yarn — ntk slope steepest, yarn flattest after kv_reserve tweak.

sarah: one more ask — let's instrument the KV eviction reason (memory pressure vs slot reassign) in metrics so we can correlate to kernel flips in dashboards. also helpful: capture head_kv_dim per model in traces.

mike: agreed. I'll add eviction_reason tag and head_kv_dim label to the kv metrics.

raj: nice work. priority: patch kernel picker + model defaults + CI sweep. aim for canary today and rollback if p95 increases >10% for any model. :thumbsup:

olivia: thanks all — filing follow-ups: PR #4523 (picker), ISSUE-987 (ci sweep), DASH-113 (kv labels). will post links once created.
